title: Dust control and damp dusting in clinical areas
audience: Cleaning staff in healthcare facilities who dust and clean floors
learningOutcomes: Describe the dust control method using a dust head kept on the floor
Explain why dry dusting is not permitted
Choose the correct damp dusting product for a surface

instruction.heading: Dust control on floors
instruction.body: Dust control uses a head that stays touching the floor during the pass. Make figure-eight passes that overlap, starting at the far end of the area and moving toward the door. Lift and remove large litter by hand first, and scrape gum off the floor before the pass. Keep the head in contact throughout, so that dust is held rather than thrown up. Once it is full, swap the head out and send it for laundering or disposal under local policy.

instruction.heading: Why dry dusting is not permitted
instruction.body: Dry dusting lifts particles back into the air instead of removing them. The Irish manual says plainly that dry dusting is not allowed. In its place, the cleaner damp dusts. Routine damp dusting uses detergent and water, not chemical disinfectant. The cloth is turned often and rinsed, the solution is changed when it turns dirty, and a dry cloth is used at the end where a surface needs it.

instruction.heading: Choosing a product for the surface
instruction.body: For most general surfaces, warm water with a detergent is the default. Alcohol wipes can decontaminate some equipment, but they can damage other items and are unsuitable where soil is visible. Detergent wipes may suit some items, following the maker's instructions. The SA standard adds that a damp cloth is the expected tool for dusting, and that brooms and feather dusters should be kept out of healthcare areas.

procedure: Remove large litter by hand before dusting.
Attach a clean dust control head and keep it on the floor throughout the pass.
Make figure-eight passes that overlap from the far end toward the door.
Replace or launder the head when it is full.
Damp-dust surfaces top to bottom using a damp cloth and detergent solution.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner has only a dry duster and finds a corridor full of dust shortly before a clinical visit.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the correct method for this corridor and its surfaces?
workedExamples.reasoning: Dry dusting is not permitted. Use a dust control head on the floor, then damp-dust the surfaces with a detergent solution, starting with the highest surfaces. Dust is removed rather than redistributed, which is the purpose of the method.

equipmentAndPpe: Detergent solution made to the label

commonErrors.error: Sweeping with a broom in patient areas
commonErrors.prevention: Use a dust control head or a damp mop instead.

commonErrors.error: Using chemical disinfectant for routine damp dusting
commonErrors.prevention: Routine damp dusting uses detergent. Disinfectant is used only where the schedule calls for it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Dust control and damp dusting method statements are from the Irish manual (2006). Where they differ from the SA standard, the SA standard's method rules apply.
Follow the product label and SDS for any detergent or wipe used.

qualityStandard: The learner describes the dust control method with the head kept on the floor
The learner states why dry dusting is not used
documentationEvidence: Cleaning checklist showing the dust control and damp dusting steps completed
summary: Dust control holds dust on a head kept touching the floor
Dry dusting is not permitted in these areas
Routine damp dusting uses detergent, and disinfectant only where the schedule calls for it

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is dry dusting prohibited in these areas?
options: It takes too long and it wastes a lot of cloth and time
It lifts particles back into the air instead of removing them
It damages the paint and the surfaces look dull and worn

knowledgeChecks.question: What should routine damp dusting use?
options: A chemical disinfectant every time on the dry surface first
Detergent and water, with the solution changed when it turns dirty
Ethanol wipes only, applied to a dry surface each time

knowledgeChecks.question: In which direction should dust control passes move?
options: From the door toward the far end
From the far end toward the door, in overlapping passes
From the door toward the window, in one pass with no overlap
